title: A bench to wear materials down

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: To study how a surface wears, you first have to wear one out, the same way every time. That takes a machine, and this repository holds the parts for it.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: So it's a machine for scuffing things on purpose?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Pretty much. WearMachine collects the parts of the abrasion bench used in Antoine's master's research at ÉTS on wear in texture space. A sample slides on a rail under a chosen load, then it's scanned with a GelSight sensor.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: And the repository is the blueprint?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The custom fixtures, yes: STEP files you can edit, STL files ready to print, DXF outlines for flat cutting, and drawing sheets. It's published under ETSim for anyone who wants to rebuild or adapt the rig, to evaluate wear, study friction or check simulations against measurements.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Three families. The rail family has the rails, the end pieces, a pusher and a bracket for a stepper motor. The weight family has holders for ten, twenty, fifty, a hundred, two hundred, five hundred and a thousand grams. And the GelSight family has holders that keep a sample under the sensor.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Each holder sets the normal load on a sample, so a test is repeatable. Pick the weight, slide the sample, scan it, and compare.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Can I see what it looks like?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The page has a 3D viewer you can orbit and zoom, with the rail parts in blue, the weight holders in orange and the sample holders in green. There are also drawings, including an assembly sheet dated March 2025 showing two rails and a crossbar with five sample holes of increasing size.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: And the samples that come out of it?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Surfaces measured with this kind of test are published in another project, WearSurfacesDatasets, with loads from ten to two hundred grams. So the bench makes the wear, and the dataset keeps the scans.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: There's nothing to run. Open the STEP files in a CAD tool to change dimensions, slice the STL files to print them, or use the DXF files for laser cutting. The written page has the full parts table and the drawings.
